title: Deep learning and spectroscopy confirm four faint quasars at redshift about 5
summary: A deep-learning and Bayesian-information-criterion search of Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam photometry selected four faint high-redshift quasar candidates. Palomar spectroscopy found broad Lyman-alpha emission and breaks in all four, confirming redshifts between 4.7 and 5.6; one object also received a black-hole mass estimate.
ai_technology: Deep-learning photometric classifier combined with Bayesian information criterion
organization: Seoul National University; Kyungpook National University; Kavli Institute for Astronomy and Astrophysics, Peking University

evidence.tested: A deep-learning and Bayesian-information-criterion search of Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam photometry selected four faint high-redshift quasar candidates.
evidence.unknown: The paper spectroscopically confirms four targeted candidates, not the full 35-object catalog. The selection method combines deep learning with a Bayesian information criterion and conventional candidate filtering; AI was one component rather than the sole discovery mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: The classifier shortlisted high-redshift quasar candidates from survey photometry; human researchers selected four for observation and used telescope spectra to confirm all four as quasars.
